text:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: alert fired - AI-HOSTED-LATENCY (service: hosted-inference) at 1769123456
pagerduty: PagerDuty: Incident PD-4987 created and notified oncall schedule alpha
maya: saw it, paging came through my phone. looking at dashboard now.
eric: same, there's a spike in p50/p95 tokens across a few regions. not sure if noise yet.
lina: any customer-facing errors? support channel empty so far.
maya: no 5xx in logs, just elevated queue time on host-gateway. plotting traces.
oncall-bot: Alert repeated 2 times in 3m (auto-escalation pending)
jon: can someone run a quick query to see if dedicated pools are affected?
eric: running: ```SELECT region, pool_type, avg(latency_ms) FROM metrics.requests WHERE ts > now() - 10m GROUP BY 1,2;```
jon: thanks
eric: results: hosted-us-west increased p95 ~300ms -> 900ms, dedicated pools unaffected (<=120ms)
sarah: looks like a noisy upstream in front of hosted router, maybe burst of long-tail requests.
maya: can we temporarily bump alert noise threshold or suppress repeats? this is spamming PD.
lina: +1, PD is close to auto-escalation. we should ack and mute repeats while we investigate.
pagerduty: PagerDuty: Incident PD-4987 acknowledged by maya at 1769123462
maya: acking. I'm going to add a suppression for 10m on the repeated rule.
oncall-bot: Command executed: `suppress-alert AI-HOSTED-LATENCY --duration 10m --reason "transient spike investigation"`
eric: adding a quick mitigation — scaling gateway pool by +2 nodes in us-west to reduce queueing. ```aws autoscaling set-desired-capacity --auto-scaling-group gateway-us-west --desired-capacity 6```
jon: will that change routing? might add latency while nodes warm.
eric: should be fine, this gateway pool has warm containers; expected <30s impact.
maya: checking trace IDs for the spike, finding a pattern: a single customer integration sent a batch storm. opening support DM to confirm if they were testing.
sarah: if it is a single noisy customer we can block or throttle their IP at the edge quickly.
lina: @maya if confirmed, do that and notify support to coordinate.
maya: confirmed via support DM—staging client accidentally replayed a job. blocking their API key for 5m. ```curl -X POST https://admin.internal/keys/block -d '{"key":"stg-client-42","ttl":"5m"}'```
oncall-bot: System: API key stg-client-42 flagged as blocked at 1769123478
eric: after block p95 in us-west dropped to ~180ms within 40s. graphs look back to normal.
jon: nice. any customer impact?
lina: Dedicated customers unaffected per earlier query. hosted customers had degraded latency for ~3-4m window; no error rate increase.
sarah: recommend we mark as "no customer-facing errors" but note degraded latency for hosted during spike window.
maya: filing follow-up ticket and tagging platform and platform-ops to review guardrails for noisy clients. I'll also request a tweak to the PD rule to require 3 successive windows before page for this metric.
eric: agree on changing to 3-window before page for this rule, with alert to slack instead of PD for first repeat.
oncall-bot: PagerDuty: PD-4987 resolved by maya at 1769123505
maya: resolving. created ticket PLAT-1293 with details and remediation steps. CC @platform @support.
jon: thanks team. can we do a quick post-mortem next standup? short blameless note.
lina: will add to incident board and assign action owners.
sarah: small ask: add automated detection for bursty API key behavior so we can throttle earlier.
maya: noted in PLAT-1293. closing thread. :thumbsup:
